# Citation

Wick, R. R. (2019). *Badread: simulation of error-prone long reads*. Journal of Open Source Software. DOI: 10.21105/joss.01316. Source: [https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.01316.pdf](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.01316.pdf).

# One-Sentence Summary

Describes Badread, a configurable simulator for error-prone long sequencing reads.

# Scope for simitall

Document as an alternative long-read simulator when users need configurable read length, identity, chimeras, or adapter artifacts beyond a PBSIM workflow.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Long-read benchmarks are sensitive to read-length and error distributions.
- Chimeras and artifact settings can create more challenging assembly conditions.
- A simulation scenario should state whether it aims for idealized or stress-test data.

# Inputs to Specify

- Reference FASTA
- Read-length, identity, and artifact models
- Coverage and random seed

# Expected Outputs

- Simulated long-read FASTQ
- Scenario parameter record

# Limitations and Guardrails

- More complex error models are not automatically more realistic for every instrument or sample.
- Choose parameters from matched empirical data when possible.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- When is Badread preferable to PBSIM for a long-read benchmark?
- How should an assembly stress-test scenario be reported?
